content:
Wow。Samsung has been leading Apple in the foldable phone market for seven years, and this time the company truly lives up to its philosophy—waiting until it can deliver something significantly better than the rest before making its move. And with the iPhone Duo, it has certainly delivered!

It's clear that Apple has carefully considered every detail of a foldable iPhone and fully leveraged every advantage this form factor offers...

Let's start with the basics. Previous reports mentioned that Apple waited until it could make the crease almost invisible and ensured the hinge design was sturdy enough to withstand countless openings and closings. While the latter remains to be verified, you can already see how much effort went into the hinge design from looking at it.

There's also the under-display front camera—visible when you need it, nearly invisible when you don't.

Apple also considered the various ways you might hold or place the device, and how software could best take advantage of these postures.

I don't remember who first said this, but I think it's absolutely right: great design is something others can't think of, but seems obvious in hindsight. The original iPhone is a perfect example. Other smartphones had physical keyboards and required *a stylus to use, but the iPhone let you use your finger, with the keyboard only appearing when needed. In hindsight, smartphones were always meant to work this way.

*Yes, the Duo supports Apple Pencil, but it's not required.

For me, the Duo keynote was full of examples like these. Why would we specifically isolate the subject from a photo and copy-paste it into another app, when you could just drag it directly from the original? In hindsight, this approach is so obvious.

Replacing the selfie timer with a method that 'automatically takes the photo when everyone stops moving.' So obvious!

Top Liked Comment by Jordan

I think Apple's marketing and visual design, as always, is truly top-notch. My immediate reaction is usually: cool, I want one. But then reality kicks in—especially with this device, the $2,000 price tag makes the decision easy, and with tight supply, it's expected to be out of stock until early 2027... Prices have gone up across the board, even for refurbished units. While this is becoming the norm, it really takes the shine off things—that's just my personal view... I used to tell people that buying a phone upgrade should be like buying a car—invest in one and use it for years. Now it seems that advice is even more fitting, because phones are about to become as expensive as cars!

There are also some UI features that have no real practical use but look beautiful, like the blur effect when you fold the device.

I could go on, but to sum up, my expectations for this device were extremely high, yet I'm still deeply impressed by its performance. I'm British, and we usually use 'wow' sarcastically—but I still want to use this word to open this article with absolutely zero sarcasm.

This device isn't actually the best fit for me. For me, an iPhone is roughly 50% ultra-slim camera, 49% pocket computer, and 1% phone. The iPhone 18 Pro Max would suit my needs much better. Still, I'm extremely tempted by the iPhone Duo.

Speaking of which, I should mention 'Apple's slightly worst quality' as referenced in the headline. Apple is brilliant at producing product videos that make you feel you could reach through the screen and touch the device. Apple can create a strong desire to buy a product we fundamentally shouldn't purchase. Although I'm not the target audience for the iPhone Duo, I truly, absolutely, undoubtedly want one. How about you?
